whats_connected.one_business_rule: Only this business's accounts are used. Accounts in another brand, a second site, another business's GA4 properties and Google Ads account, test and placeholder accounts, an ad account whose name matches neither the business nor its owner (until the user claims it), and the social scheduler's third-party accounts are left out.

snapshot.change: sessions x13 (a tracking change, not growth: see rule 2)

same_days_as_search_console.call: the same get_report, 2026-09-06 to 2026-10-03 (Search Console's last day), for rule 2

snapshot.call: get_report by eventName (keyEvents, eventCount), current window
snapshot.reading: 8 events fire; none is marked as a key event, and no sign-up event exists. One form_start fired; no form submit was recorded.

snapshot.call: search_analytics by date, both windows in one call
snapshot.change: clicks per day +8%, impressions per day -17%

snapshot.result: Not run: no Google Ads account belongs to this business. Of the brand's two, one is another business's account and one is a test account; the other three sit in another brand. (When the skill was built, this exact call was tested on the other business's account and worked; none of its numbers are used here.)

snapshot.call: get_insights_adaccount, level account, the 2 active ad accounts named for the business or its owner
snapshot.result: No delivery in either window: every call returned an empty list (spend 0). A third active ad account has a name that matches neither, so it was left out until the user says it's theirs.

diagnosis: You asked where to start on sign-ups. The data says sign-ups aren't counted anywhere yet: GA4 has no key events and no sign-up event, and over the same 28 days it records only 6% of the organic clicks Search Console reports. Organic search is your one working channel (about 60 clicks a day, +8% per day against the prior window); the Meta and LinkedIn ad accounts haven't delivered in 60 days, and there's no Google Ads account. Fix measurement first, then grow organic and the sign-up flow.

rules.name: The goal isn't measured
rules.evidence: 0 key events in both windows; no sign-up event among the 8 events GA4 records.

rules.name: GA4 misses traffic
rules.evidence: GA4 counted 110 Organic Search sessions against 1700 Search Console clicks over the same 28 days, 2026-09-06 to 2026-10-03 (6%). GA4 sessions went from 44 to 570 while organic clicks per day moved +8%.

rules.name: A fifth or more of sessions can't be placed
rules.evidence: Unassigned and zero-engagement channels (Unassigned, Cross-network, Referral) hold 23% of sessions.

rules.name: Ads spend with few or no conversions
rules.evidence: Not fired on the platforms checked: there is no Google Ads account for this business, and its Meta and LinkedIn ad accounts didn't deliver in 60 days. Microsoft Ads and the other connected ad platforms weren't read (see unknowns and question 3).

rules.name: Traffic fell more than 20%
rules.evidence: Search Console clicks per day +8% (GA4 sessions not used: rule 2 fired). Impressions per day -17%, worth watching but below the line.

rules.name: Traffic holds but key events are low
rules.evidence: Can't be graded until sign-ups are counted (rule 1).

rules.name: No clear reason to choose them
Then grow toward the goal
rules.evidence: After the measurement steps: organic search is the only channel with steady demand, and the goal is sign-ups.

layer_check.evidence: 0 key events in both windows; no sign-up event among the 8 events GA4 records. Over the same 28 days, GA4 sees 6% of the organic clicks Search Console reports.
No data source for positioning; asked below.
Organic clicks per day +8%, but impressions per day -17%.
26% of GA4 sessions engaged; conversion can't be graded.

Organic search is the only active channel among those checked; the Meta and LinkedIn ad accounts are idle for 60 days. GA4 shows 18 Paid Search sessions; Microsoft Ads is connected but not in this snapshot.
Not graded until layers 0 to 4 hold.

plan.produces: a sign-up event counted as a key event, with the fixes to get there
plan.why_here: Rule 1: a sign-up is never counted, so no later step could show it worked.

plan.produces: the settings or pages that keep GA4 from seeing organic visits, and the fixes
plan.why_here: Rule 2: over the same 28 days, GA4 records 6% of the organic clicks Search Console sees; find which pages or settings drop the rest.
plan.input_from_previous: the sign-up event defined in step 1

plan.produces: tagging rules and fixes that move Unassigned sessions into real channels
plan.why_here: Rule 3: 23% of sessions land in Unassigned or zero-engagement channels.
plan.input_from_previous: a GA4 property that counts all traffic (step 2)

plan.produces: the queries just off page one and the page changes to lift them
plan.why_here: Rule 8: organic search is the one channel with steady demand, and Search Console data isn't affected by the GA4 gaps.

plan.produces: where people drop out of sign-up, and the changes to test first
plan.why_here: The goal is sign-ups. Once step 1 counts them, the sign-up flow is where more traffic turns into more sign-ups.
plan.input_from_previous: the sign-up event (step 1) and two weeks of clean data

quick_win.why: It runs today on Search Console alone, which the GA4 problems don't touch, and it works on the channel that already brings traffic.

automate.condition: only after step 1, so the digest includes sign-ups

not_now.reason: no Google Ads account belongs to this business, and its Meta and LinkedIn ad accounts haven't delivered in 60 days; if the Paid Search traffic is Microsoft Ads (question 3), pacing comes back in

put_on_a_schedule.how: Any scheduler that can start Claude with a saved prompt, for example a scheduled task in Claude Code. The prompt is the skill name, the site and the window.

questions: Where does sign-up happen: on this site, or in a separate app on another domain? That decides where the sign-up event goes in step 1.
Can you say in one sentence why a customer picks you over the alternatives? If not, usp-extractor goes before step 4.
Is the GA4 Paid Search traffic from the connected Microsoft Ads account? If ads are planned, microsoft-ads-account-audit (Soon) joins the plan after step 3.
unknowns: Foundation layer: no data source; asked above.
Conversion rate: can't be graded until sign-ups are counted.
Microsoft Ads, TikTok Ads, Pinterest, Snapchat, X and ChatGPT Ads: connected but not read in this snapshot, so whether they spend is unknown; their own skills read them.
One more active Meta ad account has a name that matches neither the business nor its owner: left out; say if it belongs to this business.
